title: FILTERING_PROCEDURES_FOR_SENSOR_DATA_IN
universal_lens: The filtering procedure establishes a rigorous isomorphism between raw kinematic time-series and discrete topological event spaces. By applying velocity thresholds and spatial constraints to continuous sensor data, the algorithm projects high-dimensional player trajectories onto a reduced manifold of active game states, effectively separating signal from structural noise.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps this trajectory reduction into a Bayesian state-space framework. The algorithm's velocity threshold acts as a likelihood function for active play, while conformal inference bounds the uncertainty of offensive/defensive labels derived purely from geometric centroid shifts in the absence of ground-truth event logs.
gse_mapping: In GSE, the algorithm dictates the situational reasoning engine's state-transition logic. Continuous kinematic streams are discretized into valid game ticks via strict topological constraints (e.g., exactly five agents on court), ensuring the tactical simulation only processes dynamically relevant, non-degenerate spatial configurations.

primitives.name: Active Play Velocity Filter
primitives.verbatim_quote: Starting from a data matrix that tracks the movements of the players on the court at different moments in the game, we propose an algorithm to automatically drop inactive moments making use of available sensor data.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: v: instantaneous velocity (km/h); h2: minimum velocity threshold (km/h); h3: temporal persistence window (s)
primitives.assumptions: Player movement strictly adheres to classical kinematics; stationary phases correspond exclusively to dead-ball or inactive game states.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails during static set-piece plays or deliberate defensive spacing where collective velocity drops below h2 despite active gameplay.

layer2.mapping: Maps continuous kinematic vectors to a binary active/inactive state space using a persistent Heaviside step function over the velocity norm.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of dropped timestamps matching official stoppage clocks.

primitives.name: Court Occupancy Projection
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this paper we develop a data cleaning procedure for basketball which is based on players' trajectories.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: N: number of tracked agents (dimensionless); N_req: required active agents = 5 (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: A valid basketball possession requires exactly ten agents (five per team) actively tracked within the defined court boundaries.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities occur during technical fouls, injuries, or ejections resulting in asymmetric team sizes (N != 10).

layer2.mapping: Projects the full tracking matrix X onto a subspace where the cardinality of active spatial coordinates equals the regulation team size.
layer2.telemetry: Count of rows discarded due to missing GPS pings or off-court agent tracking.

primitives.name: Possession Polarity Labeling
primitives.verbatim_quote: The algorithm also divides the game into sorted actions and labels them as offensive or defensive.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: x_i, y_i: Cartesian coordinates of player i (meters); C_court: geometric center of the basketball court (meters)
primitives.assumptions: Offensive and defensive teams maintain distinct, separable spatial centroids relative to the court's longitudinal axis during active play.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down during fast-break transitions or chaotic turnovers where spatial clustering of opposing teams overlaps significantly.

layer2.mapping: Assigns a discrete polarity label (+1/-1) to a temporal segment by evaluating the signed distance of the team's spatial centroid from C_court.
layer2.telemetry: Label accuracy against manually annotated possession changes.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation begins with a high-frequency spatio-temporal matrix X representing continuous player trajectories. To extract meaningful tactical primitives, we must first eliminate structural noise inherent in sports data, such as timeouts, free throws, and halftime intervals. The proposed operator employs a multi-stage filtration process grounded in kinematic constraints. First, a cardinality constraint ensures exactly five players per team are present, projecting X onto a valid game-state manifold. Second, a velocity-based filter utilizes a persistent threshold (h2, h3) to excise temporally contiguous segments where kinetic energy approaches zero, effectively isolating active play from dead-ball situations. Third, spatial heuristics identify and remove isolated events like free throws based on rigid coordinate positioning. Once the matrix is reduced to active temporal slices, a secondary operator performs action segmentation. By calculating the average spatial positioning (centroid) of the five active players relative to the court's geometry, the algorithm assigns a polarity label—offensive or defensive. This transforms unstructured sensor telemetry into a sorted sequence of discrete tactical actions. The dualities lie in the transition from continuous differential kinematics to discrete topological event labeling. Failure modes emerge when tactical stasis mimics dead-ball conditions, or when rapid transitions blur the spatial separation required for accurate polarity assignment.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This methodology inherits its mathematical lineage from ecological dynamics and complex systems theory, specifically the works of Davids and Araujo on team sports complexity. It bridges the gap between raw Information Technology outputs and Social Network Analysis (SNA) centrality measures. Historically, it evolves from basic activity recognition algorithms, adapting continuous wavelet transforms and thresholding techniques originally designed for biomechanical gait analysis into the highly constrained, multi-agent topology of professional basketball.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The algorithm implicitly models the decision actors—coaches and players—as bounded rational agents operating under strict spatial and temporal constraints. By relying solely on GPS accelerometry, the system infers the collective intent of these agents without access to their internal cognitive states or explicit rule-book annotations. It assumes that the physical manifestation of a coach's strategy (e.g., a defensive set) will inevitably produce a distinct, measurable spatial signature among the five executing players, allowing the machine to reverse-engineer the tactical 'mind' from pure kinematics.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: To prevent anti-collinearity and leakage between layers, strict veto conditions must be applied. If the spatial variance of the five-player centroid falls below a minimal dispersion threshold, the offensive/defensive labeling operator must be suspended, as clustered positions yield ambiguous polarity. Furthermore, if the velocity filter drops more than a statistically anomalous percentage of frames within a single quarter, a systemic sensor failure is flagged, vetoing the entire segment from downstream GSI inference to prevent propagating corrupted state transitions into the tactical engine.
